candidate_requirements.requirement: Request renal function and quantify/characterise the urine abnormality.
candidate_requirements.rationale: Persistent abnormal urinalysis and proteinuria require establishing renal severity and whether the pattern suggests glomerular or tubular involvement.
candidate_requirements.acceptable_alternatives: Creatinine/eGFR plus protein quantification and urinalysis or appropriate tubular-protein assessment. Clinically equivalent urine/renal work-up counts; exhaustive tubular testing is not required.
candidate_requirements.deadline: Before the final assessment, within the six question turns.

candidate_requirements.requirement: Request monoclonal-protein testing or an equivalent haematological evaluation.
candidate_requirements.rationale: The task explicitly asks whether haematological evidence changes the renal differential; a defensible assessment needs the relevant protein evidence.
candidate_requirements.acceptable_alternatives: Serum/urine electrophoresis with immunofixation and/or serum free light chains, or an appropriate paraprotein work-up. No need to name a hidden renal lesion.
candidate_requirements.deadline: Before the final assessment, within the six question turns.

candidate_requirements.requirement: Seek evidence of systemic clonal disease and a discriminating tissue/tubular assessment.
candidate_requirements.rationale: Monoclonal-protein findings do not by themselves identify the renal lesion or establish the full systemic disease category.
candidate_requirements.acceptable_alternatives: Marrow or skeletal assessment, renal biopsy planning, simultaneous glucose or clinically equivalent proximal-tubular studies. Adequate requests count even when their results are withheld.
candidate_requirements.deadline: Before the final assessment, within the six question turns.
